title: FactorIA model document (*.model.json)
description: A 3D model as a tree of operations (primitives, modifiers, organic `sdf` shapes, groups, transforms) with named parts, materials and vertex colours. `model.bake` evaluates it and writes the .glb next to it; the same bytes on every platform. Errors name the file and the JSON pointer; docs/MODELING.md explains the format and `model.info {}` lists the operations.

doc.description: What the model is and where the game uses it.

path.description: Project-relative file under assets/ ending in .glb. Left out: next to the document, with .glb instead of .model.json.

materials.description: Named materials the nodes refer to with `material`.

additionalProperties.description: A material, named by its key in `materials`. Written into the .glb as a glTF material.

color.description: Base colour [r, g, b, a], 0..1. Default white.

texture.description: A project image used as the base colour texture, e.g. "assets/textures/wood.png". The model's uvs are per primitive (docs/MODELING.md).

emissive.description: Light the surface gives off [r, g, b], 0..1. Default none.

doubleSided.description: Draw back faces too (flat leaves, cloth). Default false.

blend.description: Alpha-blended (glass); the alpha of `color` and of vertex colours shows. Default false.

nodes.description: The tree: operations evaluated in order and merged into one mesh.

box.description: A box centred on its origin; its faces are grids when `segments` is above 1. The size is X (width), Y (height), Z (depth).

id.description: A name for this node that stays the same when the tree changes: model.edit finds nodes by it. Letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.`, at most 64 characters, unique in the document.

note.description: A comment for the next person (or AI) reading the document; it has no effect.

enabled.description: false leaves the node (and everything below it) out without deleting it.

part.description: The part of the model this node and the nodes below it belong to ("door", "left_wheel"). Parts become submeshes of the baked .glb, named in the primitive's extras, so tools and scripts can find them. Left out: the part of the group above, else none.

material.description: A key of the document's `materials`. Left out: the material of the group above, else the default (white). Nodes with the same part and material share a submesh.

color.description: Vertex colour, [r, g, b] or [r, g, b, a] in 0..1, or "#rrggbb" / "#rrggbbaa". Multiplies the material's colour when drawn. Left out: the colour of the group above, else none.

sweep.description: A closed profile moved along a path: a pipe, a rail, a rope, a road edge, a handle. It is a primitive: `align` places it.

sdf.description: Organic shapes by signed distance fields instead of triangles: its `children` (`sdf_sphere`, `sdf_capsule`, `sdf_ellipsoid`, `sdf_box`, `sdf_cylinder`, `sdf_cone`, `sdf_torus`, `sdf_group`) describe a solid, joined in order with union, subtraction or intersection and a blend distance that melts them into each other (a creature, a rock, a tree, a mushroom, a prop that looks grown rather than assembled). The solid is meshed on a grid (marching tetrahedra: always a closed manifold surface), decimated with a quadric error metric that keeps the part boundaries, and given smooth normals from the field. The result is an ordinary mesh node: `align` and the transform place it, modifiers can wrap it and a boolean can take it as an operand. Each shape's `part`, `material` and `color` are kept: a triangle belongs to the part of the shape that owns the surface there, a vertex colour melts across a smooth blend.

face_selection.description: A choice of faces by meaning, evaluated on the mesh at this point of the tree (never indices): `by` says how, the other fields depend on it. "all": Every face. "part": The faces of one or more parts (the `part` names of the nodes that made them; "" is the faces of nodes that name no part). A face keeps its part through extrusions and modifiers. "normal": The faces that point in a direction: the angle between the face's normal and `direction` is at most `tolerance`. {"by": "normal", "direction": "top"} picks the upward-facing faces of a box. "top": The highest faces along an axis: the faces whose centre is within `within` of the highest face centre. The cap of a cylinder, the top row of a wall, the faces around a sphere's pole. Unlike `normal` it picks by position, so it finds the top of a part whatever way its faces point; give `of` to look only among some faces (the top of the part "body"). "bottom": The lowest faces along an axis: the faces whose centre is within `within` of the lowest face centre. The cap of a cylinder, the top row of a wall, the faces around a sphere's pole. Unlike `normal` it picks by position, so it finds the bottom of a part whatever way its faces point; give `of` to look only among some faces (the bottom of the part "body"). "box": The faces inside an axis-aligned box. "sphere": The faces inside a ball. "halfspace": The faces on one side of a plane: the side `normal` points to. {"by": "halfspace", "point": [0, 0.5, 0], "normal": [0, 1, 0]} is everything above y = 0.5. "and": The faces that every query in `of` chooses. "or": The faces that any query in `of` chooses. "not": Every face that `of` does not choose. "grow": The faces `of` chooses plus the faces that share an edge with them, `steps` times. "shrink": The faces `of` chooses minus the ones on its border (the faces with an edge shared with a face that is not chosen), `steps` times.
